card.title: Average Translational Kinetic Energy of Gas Molecule

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Equating the kinetic-theory pressure $P = \frac{1}{3}\frac{Nm}{V}\bar{c^2}$ with the gas equation $PV = Nk_BT$ gives $\frac{1}{2}m\bar{c^2} = \frac{3}{2}k_BT$: the **average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule depends only on absolute temperature** — $\frac{3}{2}k_BT$ per molecule, $\frac{3}{2}RT$ per mole, $\frac{3}{2}nRT$ total for a monatomic ideal gas.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - KE = (3/2)k_BT (per molecule) - KE = (3/2)RT (per mole) - U = (3/2)nRT (monatomic ideal gas)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Equipartition Result:** The average translational kinetic energy per molecule is $\langle KE_{trans} angle = rac{3}{2} k_B T = rac{3}{2} rac{R}{N_A} T$. This comes from 3 translational degrees of freedom, each contributing $ rac{1}{2} k_B T$ via equipartition.  ·  **Temperature Proportionality:** $\langle KE_{trans} angle \propto T$ — absolute temperature is a direct measure of average translational kinetic energy. This is why Kelvin scale is fundamental: at $T=0$, translational KE is zero (classically).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Do not confuse kB per molecule with R per mole.  ·  Polyatomic-gas internal energy may include rotational and vibrational modes.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Per molecule use k_B; per mole use R** — the factor-1000 trap.  ·  **KE depends only on T** — hydrogen and oxygen molecules at the same T carry the same average translational KE.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Find mean translational energy per molecule at 400 K using kB=1.38×10⁻²³ J K⁻¹.  ·  Why do lighter molecules move faster at the same temperature?

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (2m): Find the average KE per molecule at 27 °C.** — T = 300 K → KE = 6.21×10⁻²¹ J (same as 2024's answer).

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: A 2m plug-in; the derivation (3m) may also be asked.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Temperature IS molecular kinetic energy** — the deepest statement of kinetic theory.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: At absolute zero, translational molecular motion ceases — that is what 0 K means.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Temperature Is Energy Match the kinetic-theory pressure to the ideal gas equation and temperature stops being a thermometer reading: it becomes the average translational kinetic energy of molecules, $\frac{3}{2}k_BT$ per molecule. At 300 K every molecule — any gas, any mass — carries exactly 6.2×10⁻²¹ J of translational energy.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2024) ### 2.1 Derivation From the pressure derivation: $P = \frac{1}{3}\frac{Nm}{V}\bar{c^2}$, and the ideal gas equation $PV = Nk_BT$: $$\frac{1}{3}\frac{Nm}{V}\bar{c^2} \cdot V = Nk_BT \Rightarrow \frac{1}{3}m\bar{c^2} = k_BT$$ $$\boxed{\bar{KE}_{trans} = \frac{1}{2}m\bar{c^2} = \frac{3}{2}k_BT}$$ — depends **only on temperature**, not on the…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 64:** one-line consequence of matching the two pressure expressions. - **To equipartition (Topic 67):** the ½k_BT per degree of freedom generalises this. - **To absolute zero:** at T = 0 translational KE vanishes — the physical meaning of absolute zero.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Internal Energy of Monatomic Gas:** For a monatomic ideal gas, $U = N \langle KE_{trans} angle = rac{3}{2} nRT$. The internal energy is purely translational KE. For diatomic/polyatomic gases, $U$ includes rotational and vibrational contributions as well.  ·  Verified PYQ: KE per molecule at 300 K (2024, 2m).  ·  "The average translational kinetic energy of a gas molecule is directly proportional to the absolute temperature."
